content:
jules: hey — running into a weird bug in the sampleapp onboarding steps when the worker spins up. we call our wrapper that ends up calling `asyncio.run()` and it crashes with 'asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop'
jules: repro (minimal):
```python
# in a background thread started by the sampleapp CLI
import asyncio
import httpx

def background_job():
    async def work():
        async with httpx.AsyncClient() as c:
            await c.get('https://example.com')
    asyncio.run(work())  # <-- fails if there's already a running loop

# CLI spawns thread that itself is in an event loop (uvicorn/process manager)
```
priya: can you paste the exact stacktrace? sounds like the CLI or test harness already created a loop
jules: stacktrace snippet:
```
RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
  File ".../sampleapp/worker.py", line 42, in background_job
    asyncio.run(work())
```
simon: yep — classic. library code (or our wrapper) should never call `asyncio.run()` unconditionally. that assumes you own the main loop. for SDKs you should *detect* running loop and either expose async/sync APIs or use `anyio` helpers.
priya: is the failure specifically about `asyncio.run` or about reusing httpx clients across threads? we've also seen "attached to a different loop" with `AsyncClient` objects.
jules: good call — also saw `RuntimeError: Task got Future attached to a different loop` in a separate run when we cached the client in a global and threads reused it.
amanda: short-term workaround: make the sample CLI call the sync `httpx.Client` from threads, or create a new loop per-thread and use `asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)` before `asyncio.run` — but both are hacks.
simon: longer-term: change SDK to offer two explicit entrypoints: `Client` (sync) and `AsyncClient` (async). Internally implement a tiny shim for sync code that calls `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` or uses `trio`/`anyio` to be loop-agnostic. avoid `asyncio.run()` inside library code.
jules: agree. currently our wrapper `redwood_sdk.sync_request` does `asyncio.run(self._async_request(...))` which is the root cause for users embedding SDK into existing async apps.
priya: can we add a runtime-detect patch now: if `asyncio.get_running_loop()` exists, detect and use `anyio.from_thread.run` path instead of `asyncio.run()`? minimal conditional until proper API split.
amanda: i'll draft a patch. will also add a dev note in the onboarding sample about "if your app is async, use AsyncClient; do not call sample CLI which uses threads" — saves new users.
dev-tools-bot: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1456 — "avoid asyncio.run in sync wrapper; add loop-aware shim" — assigned to @amanda
simon: assign a follow-up to add unit tests that run our sync wrapper under an already-running loop (pytest-asyncio) and run in a threadpool to catch regressions.
jules: this blocked a partner onboarding session earlier today — thanks for the quick triage. once patch lands i'll update the sampleapp repo and ping onboarding doc owners.
priya: fwiw we should also mention common errors in the quickstarts: "if you see X, likely you called sync wrapper inside an async process" (short troubleshooting bullet)
amanda: will do. PR incoming in ~2 hours. :thumbsup:
